subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for Bluecrest — tokens/sec, SLO fit, headroom
messages:
From: Alex Trinh <alex.trinh@bluecrest.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated Plan — Bluecrest proof of scale

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this — quick summary of what we expect on day 1 of production: approximately 250 steady requests/sec for our core inference endpoint (customer-facing chat). Average request: ~320 prompt tokens, typical model-generated response: ~480 tokens. So ballpark ~800 tokens per request.

Key SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 450ms (we realize this is tight), p99 spikes tolerated if short. We care about tail for interactive sessions. Cold-cache cold-starts are OK for <1% of traffic.

Questions for you: what committed dedicated slab would you recommend to meet the SLOs with a reasonable safety buffer for surges (we expect +60% peak events during marketing campaigns)? Also let us know any assumptions you need (KV cache hit rate, batching, recommended model variants).

Attn: CC-ing our infra lead if you need system configs.

— Alex
Alex Trinh
Head of Product
Bluecrest
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Trinh <alex.trinh@bluecrest.com>
Date: 2025-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated Plan — Bluecrest proof of scale

Alex, thanks — this is a helpful starting point. Quick back-of-envelope: 250 req/s * 800 tokens/request = 200,000 tokens/sec sustained.

A couple assumptions we'll probably iterate on:
- KV cache warm hit rate (affects effective tokens generated on model path). If you can get 70% warm-hit on prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, effective model tokens/sec needs drop significantly.
- Desired model variant: are you fixed on a specific open model, or open to a smaller quantized variant for latency?
- Concurrency distribution: are those 250 steady concurrent request starts, or 250 QPS (many small concurrent flows)?

I can put together a short dedicated-slab proposal (GPU mix + headroom) and loop Eng/SE for a more accurate tokens/sec->GPU mapping. I'll also attach an initial capacity sketch for reference.

Proposed next step: internal sizing w/ Priyom (solutions) and Kimberly (pricing) and a follow-up meeting w/ your infra team.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-14T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Bluecrest dedicated sizing — quick calc and ask

Priyom / Kimberly,

Looping you in to size the Bluecrest ask. Raw numbers from customer: 250 req/s * ~800 tokens = 200k tokens/sec sustained baseline. They want p95 <= 450ms. They anticipate +60% surge windows.

My quick model mapping with Redwood throughput profiles:
- If Bluecrest uses a Mistral-7B-quant (fast, compressed variant) we observe ~45k tokens/sec sustained per H100-equivalent GPU under production batching + prefix caching assumptions (70% KV hit).
- For 13–20B-class models (higher quality), throughput drops — range ~12k–20k tok/s per H100-equivalent depending on quantization and sequence lengths.

Sizing options (sustained target + 25% operational headroom):
- Option A (performance-first): 200k tok/s sustained -> require ~5 H100-equiv @45k => 225k capacity; with 25% headroom target -> bump to 7 H100-equiv. Recommend committed slab: 8 H100-equiv to be conservative (handles 60% surge windows via autoscale + burst).
- Option B (quality-first): use 13–20B family -> assume 16k tok/s per H100-equiv -> need ~13 GPUs sustained + +25% headroom -> ~17 GPUs. This is materially larger and increases committed cost.
- Option C (hybrid): commit 6 H100-equiv for primary (balanced 13B quant) and have fallback pool of 6 A10G-equivalents for non-latency-critical background generation; use model routing: steer interactive sessions to high-perf slab and bulk tasks to cheaper pool.

Other levers:
- Increase KV cache hit from 70% -> 85% reduces model tokens/sec by ~40% effective load.
- Response streaming vs batched completions: streaming increases latency sensitivity but helps perceived responsiveness; batching increases token throughput at slight latency cost.
- Quantization to int8/4-bit yields 1.6–2.5x throughput improvement depending on model.

Pricing / deal-level recommendation (Kimberly, please confirm): proposing a reserved slab equivalent to 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (monthly commitment) with a 6–9 month ramp, including 10% burst capacity allowance and documented fallback SLAs. Attachments: bluecrest_token_model_v1.xlsx (workbook with sims) and sla_proposal_20250914.docx.

Please sanity-check numbers and suggest pricing bracket to propose.

— Sean
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Trinh <alex.trinh@bluecrest.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-18T10:09:00-07:00
Subject: Bluecrest recommended dedicated commitment (summary + next steps)

Alex — thanks for the context earlier. We ran a capacity simulation and compared three options; summary below with our recommended path to meet p95 <= 450ms and absorb ~+60% marketing surges.

Executive summary (recommendation):
- Recommended committed slab: 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (monthly reserved). Supports ~360k tokens/sec peak with our runtime profile when using Mistral-7B-quant / 70–75% KV warm-hit. That yields sustained 200k tokens/sec for baseline load and ~25% operational headroom; in practice with burst autoscaling and cached prefixes we estimate p95 generation latency < 450ms for interactive sessions.
- Fallback plan: deploy a secondary pool of up to 6 A10G-equivalent GPUs for asynchronous / lower-priority workloads, and enable automatic routing to cheaper pool for long-form generations.

Assumptions / knobs we used in the simulation:
- Avg tokens/request: 800 (your number)
- KV cache warm-hit: 70% (customer-provided)
- Model: Mistral-7B quantized to int8 (good latency/quality tradeoff) -> ~45k tok/s per H100-equiv in our profile with batching window ~8–12ms.
- Headroom target: 25% operational + 10% reserved burst for short spikes.

Operational considerations:
- We'll instrument token-level tracing and p95 dashboards in Redwood Console for your routes; initial 30-day quality monitoring included to detect regression if we change model variants or quantization.
- Recommend a 6-month committed ramp to allow you to validate traffic shape and for us to rightsize slab after month 2 using real telemetry.

Commercials: Kimberly will send a term sheet with committed GPU equivalents, discount tiers, and burst credits. If you prefer a H100-physical mapping vs mixed-A10G mapping, we can provide both pricing lines; H100 carries higher unit cost but smaller GPU count for the same tokens/sec.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly to follow up with a draft commitment and pricing (DocuSign link included).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical walkthrough next week with your infra + our solutions engineering to validate KV cache config and canary rollout plan.
3) We will share the capacity workbook and run a 72-hour synthetic spike test in a staging pool before go-live.

Links / attachments: bluecrest_token_model_v1.xlsx (capacity workbook), sla_proposal_20250914.docx, Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-example-bluecrest-capacity

If this aligns, we'll prepare the term sheet and book the technical session.

Best,
